advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a lower-bound liveness anchor (e.g. assert scans_one is above a fixed floor consistent with the documented 6-scans-for-1-child) so the equality assertion cannot pass trivially when the fingerprint scan path is skipped.
evidence: _attested_delivered denies delivery at `if sig.get("verdict") != "certified": return False` and in the `except Exception: ... return False` branch (attest_gate.py:42-48) BEFORE reaching compute_validity's fingerprint scans

The only liveness anchor is `assert manifest == []` (line 91), which is satisfied by ANY denial path, including denial paths that perform zero full-store scans — so a `0 == 0` result is indistinguishable from a genuine constant-scan pass
ABSENCE: no assertion of the form `assert scans_one >= N` or `assert scans_one > 0` that would confirm the completion/fingerprint scan path actually ran
advisory.finding: The scan-count regression test asserts equality (scans_four == scans_one) but never asserts a lower bound on scans_one, so if the expensive fingerprint scan path stops executing (e.g. verify_signature stops returning 'certified', delivery is denied at the pre-fingerprint early return in _attested_delivered, or an exception is swallowed), both counts collapse to an equal small constant and the equality passes trivially — the test then reports green whether or not the O(N)->O(1) collapse under review is actually exercised.
scenarios: A future change makes the completion branch short-circuit before live_material_children; scan counts drop to a small equal constant and the equality still passes, hiding a re-introduced per-child scan regression once the branch is restored

The fake verify_signature stops matching the production seam (kind mismatch or signature-shape change); denial happens at the verdict check, scans_one == scans_four == small-constant, test stays green
advisory.suggested_fix: In _scans_for_child_count or the test, assert the expensive path ran, e.g. `assert scans_one >= EXPECTED_MIN_SCANS_PER_ASSEMBLY` (a documented constant), before comparing scans_four == scans_one; this converts the equality from a fail-open oracle into one anchored on the producer having actually scanned.
